Terms of Reference: Human Resource Information System
(HRIS)
Synthetic document for a proof of concept. The company, people, figures and contact details are fictional.
Issued by: Kalinaw Trading Corporation (fictional), Human Resources and Administration Department
1. Background
1.1 About the Company
Kalinaw Trading Corporation (the "Company") is a distributor of household and hardware goods with a head
office and 12 branches in Luzon and the Visayas. The Company employs approximately 500 regular,
probationary and project-based employees. Branch staff work in fixed and rotating shifts; head office staff
work a regular day schedule.
1.2 Current situation
Human resource records are maintained by each branch in separate spreadsheets: employee personal data,
employment history, leave credits and leave balances are currently kept in spreadsheets that are consolidated
by the head office HR unit every month. Leave applications are filed on paper forms and routed for signatures.
Each branch has its own time-recording device; attendance logs are downloaded by branch staff and
summarised manually before every payroll cut-off.
This process causes late and inconsistent leave balances, disputes on attendance and overtime, duplicated
encoding at every cut-off, and limited visibility for management on headcount, attrition and attendance.
1.3 Purpose of this TOR
This Terms of Reference sets out the requirements for the design, development, deployment and turnover of a
web-based Human Resource Information System (the "System") for the Company.
1.4 Contact for this TOR
All clarifications regarding this TOR shall be submitted in writing to the designated contact person.
Contact person: [NAME], HR and Administration Manager
Email: [EMAIL]
Mobile: [MOBILE]
Clarification requests are accepted until ten (10) working days before the submission deadline.
Page 1 of 10

2. Objectives
The System shall:
1. Provide a single, accurate source of employee information for the head office and all branches.
2. Automate leave filing, approval and balance computation.
3. Bring branch attendance logs into one place and compute daily time records consistently.
4. Give employees self-service access to their own records and requests.
5. Provide attendance, overtime and leave data to the payroll process without re-encoding.
6. Give management timely dashboards and reports on the workforce.
3. Scope of Work
3.1 Functional modules
The scope covers the following modules, described in Sections 4 to 10:
- Employee information management
- Leave management
- Time and attendance
- Employee self-service
- Payroll interface
- Dashboards and reports
- Security, access control, audit trail and notifications
3.2 Technical scope
The System shall be hosted in a public cloud environment arranged by the vendor, with separate
development, test (UAT) and production environments. The System shall be accessible through current
versions of common web browsers on desktop and mobile devices.
3.3 Not in scope
- Payroll computation, withholding tax and statutory contribution processing remain in the Company's
existing payroll system and are not part of this procurement.
- Recruitment, learning management and performance appraisal modules are not part of this procurement.
- Cloud subscription fees after turnover will be paid by the Company.
3.4 Users
| User group | Approximate number |
|---|---|
| Employees (self-service) | 500 |
| Supervisors and department heads (approvers) | 60 |
| HR staff (head office and branch HR officers) | 15 |
| Management (dashboards) | 10 |
| System administrators | 2 |
Page 2 of 10

4. Employee Information Management
4.1 Employee master record
The System shall maintain a complete employee record (201 file) for every employee, including personal
information, government identification numbers, contact details, emergency contacts, dependents, educational
background, employment status, position, branch, department, immediate supervisor, date hired and
regularisation date. HR staff shall be able to create, update, search and view employee records; changes to
sensitive fields shall require HR approval. The complete employee records and current leave balances of all
employees shall be available in the System from the first day of live operation.
4.2 Organisation structure
HR staff shall maintain the Company's organisation structure: branches, departments, positions and reporting
lines. Each employee shall be assigned to one branch, one department and one position, and to an immediate
supervisor. The organisation structure shall drive the routing of approvals.
4.3 Employee documents
HR staff shall upload and maintain employee documents (employment contract, government IDs, certificates,
clearances) in PDF or image format, up to 10 MB per file. Documents with an expiry date (for example,
professional licences and health certificates) shall be tracked, and HR staff shall see a list of documents
expiring within the next 30 days.
4.4 Employment movements
The System shall record employment movements such as regularisation, promotion, transfer between
branches, change of position and separation, each with an effective date and remarks. The movement history
of each employee shall be viewable in chronological order. A movement shall update the employee's current
branch, position or status on its effective date.
Page 3 of 10

5. Leave Management
5.1 Leave types and policies
HR staff shall configure leave types (vacation leave, sick leave, emergency leave, maternity, paternity, solo
parent and special leaves for women, and leave without pay) with their entitlement rules: annual credits,
monthly accrual, eligibility after regularisation, maximum carry-over and conversion of unused credits to cash
at year-end. Leave policies may differ by employment status.
5.2 Leave application
Employees shall file leave applications online, selecting the leave type, dates (whole or half day) and reason,
and attaching supporting documents where required (for example, a medical certificate for sick leave of more
than two consecutive days). Employees may cancel a pending application or request cancellation of an
approved one.
5.3 Leave approval
Leave applications shall be approved in two levels: first by the employee's immediate supervisor, then by the
department head as final approver. Approvers shall approve, reject or return an application with remarks.
Approvals shall be possible from a mobile browser.
5.4 Leave balances
The System shall compute leave balances automatically from credits, monthly accruals, approved leaves,
carry-over and conversions. Employees and HR staff shall see the current balance per leave type and the
history of transactions. The System shall prevent filing beyond the available balance except for leave without
pay.
5.5 Holiday calendar
HR staff shall maintain a holiday calendar with regular and special non-working holidays, including local
holidays that apply only to specific branches. Holidays shall be excluded when counting leave days.
Page 4 of 10

6. Time and Attendance
6.1 Attendance capture
Attendance logs from the time-recording devices at each branch shall be brought into the System at least
once a day. Logs shall be matched to employees by employee number. Branches with connectivity problems
shall be able to upload log files manually.
6.2 Shift schedules
HR staff and branch supervisors shall maintain shift schedules and work rosters, including fixed, rotating and
flexible shifts, rest days and schedule swaps. Schedules may be assigned per employee or per group and
may be uploaded from a template.
6.3 Daily time record
The System shall compute each employee's daily time record from attendance logs and schedules: hours
worked, lates, undertime, absences, overtime hours and night differential hours, taking approved leaves and
holidays into account. HR staff shall review and lock the daily time records of each payroll cut-off.
6.4 Overtime
Employees shall file overtime requests before or after rendering overtime. Overtime requests shall be
approved by the immediate supervisor. Only approved overtime shall be counted in the daily time record.
6.5 Attendance corrections
Employees shall file correction requests for missed or wrong time entries, with a reason. Corrections shall be
approved by the immediate supervisor and shall update the daily time record once approved.
Page 5 of 10

7. Employee Self-Service
7.1 Profile and personal data updates
Employees shall view their own employee record and submit change requests for personal information
(address, contact numbers, civil status, dependents, emergency contacts) with supporting documents. HR
staff shall approve or reject each change request; approved changes shall update the employee record.
7.2 Personal views
Employees shall view their leave balances, leave history, daily time records, overtime and attendance
corrections, and their payslips for the last 12 months. Payslips are produced by the payroll system.

TOR as Small.
7.3 Certificate of employment
Employees shall request a certificate of employment, stating the purpose. HR staff shall approve the request,
and the System shall generate the certificate as a PDF from a Company template with the employee's details,
for download by the employee.
7.4 Accessibility of self-service
Self-service functions shall be usable on mobile browsers, as most branch employees do not have Company
computers.
Page 6 of 10

8. Payroll Interface
8.1 Data to payroll
At the end of every payroll cut-off, the System shall provide the Company's payroll system with each
employee's approved attendance, overtime, night differential and leave data for that cut-off. The interface shall
not require re-encoding by payroll staff.
8.2 Data from payroll
Payslip data produced by the payroll system shall be brought into the System so employees can view their
payslips under Section 7.2.
8.3 Reconciliation
The System shall keep a record of every data exchange with the payroll system, including the cut-off period,
the number of employees and the status of the exchange.
9. Dashboards and Reports
9.1 Management dashboard
Management shall have a dashboard showing headcount by branch, department and employment status; new
hires and separations; attrition rate; leave utilisation; absenteeism and tardiness rates; and overtime hours.
Users shall filter the dashboard by branch and period.
9.2 Standard reports
HR staff shall generate standard reports with export to Excel and PDF: employee masterlist, leave balances
and leave availed, attendance summary, tardiness and absences, overtime summary, employment
movements, and documents expiring.
Page 7 of 10

10. Security, Access Control, Audit and Notifications
10.1 Role-based access
Access shall be based on roles (employee, approver, branch HR officer, head office HR, management,
system administrator). Branch HR officers shall see only the employees of their own branch; head office HR
and management shall see all branches.
10.2 User administration
System administrators shall create, deactivate and reset user accounts and assign roles and branches.
Employees who are separated shall lose access on their separation date.
10.3 Audit trail
The System shall record every creation, update, deletion, approval and login, with the user, date and time,
and the values before and after the change. HR managers shall search the audit trail by user, employee and
date range.
10.4 Notifications
The System shall send email notifications for submitted, approved, rejected and returned requests, and
reminders to approvers with pending requests older than two working days. HR staff shall receive reminders
for documents expiring within 30 days.
10.5 Data privacy
The System shall seamlessly address all data privacy needs of the Company in an optimal manner.
Page 8 of 10

11. Non-Functional Requirements
11.1 Hosting
The System shall be deployed on a public cloud platform in a region acceptable to the Company, with daily
backups retained for 30 days.
11.2 Performance and availability
- The System shall support 300 concurrent users.
- Pages shall load within 3 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
- The System shall have at least 99.5% monthly availability, excluding scheduled maintenance.
11.3 General
The System shall be secure, user-friendly and scalable to support the Company's future growth. Data shall be
encrypted in transit and at rest.
12. Business Rules
12.1 Leave filing
Vacation leave shall be filed at least three (3) working days before the leave date. Sick and emergency leave
may be filed up to two (2) working days after the employee reports back to work.
12.2 Approval levels
Leave applications shall follow a three-level approval: the immediate supervisor, the department head and the
HR manager.
12.3 Overtime
Overtime of more than four (4) hours on a working day requires prior approval.
12.4 Data retention
Records of separated employees shall be retained for at least five (5) years after separation.
Page 9 of 10

13. Deliverables and Project Governance
The vendor shall deliver: project plan; business requirements and design documents; the System deployed in
the test and production environments; test scripts and results; user and administrator manuals; training for HR
staff, approvers and administrators; and source code and turnover documents. The vendor shall assign a
project manager and report status weekly. The Company shall assign a product owner from HR.
14. Commercial Terms
14.1 Contract type
The contract shall be fixed price, inclusive of all professional fees for the scope of this TOR.
14.2 Delivery period
The System shall be delivered, accepted and in live operation within five (5) months from the issuance of the
Notice to Proceed.
14.3 Payment terms
- Ten percent (10%) of the contract price upon contract signing.
- Ninety percent (90%) of the contract price upon final acceptance of the System.
14.4 Acceptance
Final acceptance is given after successful user acceptance testing and one month of live operation without
critical defects.
14.5 Warranty
The vendor shall provide a warranty of six (6) months after final acceptance, covering defect correction at no
additional cost.
15. Submission
Proposals shall include the proposed solution, project team, work plan and timeline, and the fixed price.
Proposals will be evaluated on technical merit (70%) and price (30%).
Page 10 of 10

Bid Bulletin No. 01: Human Resource Information System
(HRIS)
Synthetic document for a proof of concept. The company, people, figures and contact details are fictional.
Issued by: Kalinaw Trading Corporation (fictional), Human Resources and Administration Department
Date issued: 5 December 2026
1. Purpose
This bulletin amends the Terms of Reference for the Human Resource Information System. Where it differs
from the Terms of Reference, this bulletin governs. Prospective vendors raised questions about the number of
leave approval levels and about the delivery period, and the Company has reviewed both with its
management committee.
2. Leave approval levels
Sections 5.3 and 12.2 of the Terms of Reference stated the approval levels differently. The Company has
confirmed the following.
2.1 Approval levels
Under Section 5.3, leave applications shall be approved in three levels: first by the immediate supervisor, then
by the department head, and finally by the HR manager.
3. Delivery period
The Company recognises that the original period leaves little room for user acceptance testing and live
operation.
3.1 Revised delivery period
Under Section 14.2, the System shall be delivered, accepted and in live operation within six (6) months from
the issuance of the Notice to Proceed.
Page 1 of 2

4. Additional requirement
Employees asked to keep a personal copy of their leave history for their own records.
4.1 Leave ledger download
Under Section 5.4, employees shall be able to download their own leave ledger for the current year as a PDF
file.
5. Other provisions
All other provisions of the Terms of Reference remain in effect. Vendors should reflect this bulletin in their
proposals and acknowledge its receipt in the proposal cover letter.
Clarifications on this bulletin may be submitted in writing to the designated contact person within three (3)
working days from its date of issue. The Company does not expect to change the submission deadline as a
result of this bulletin.
Issued for and on behalf of the Company by the HR and Administration Department.
Page 2 of 2

features.route_reason: Online leave application with attachments and cancellation is a standard feature.
features.justification: Matches rubric criterion for screen_crud with file attachments and multiple fields (guideline-sizing_rubric_screen_crud)

args.query: leave application screen with leave type, dates selection, reason, attachment, cancel pending and request cancel approved

features.name: Leave approval
features.description: Approvers shall approve, reject or return an application with remarks.
features.route_reason: Leave approval workflow with remarks is a common feature.
features.justification: Single-level approval with return-for-correction loop per rubric and pattern 'patterns-single_level_approval'

args.query: leave approval workflow approve reject return application with remarks

features.name: Leave balances
features.description: The System shall compute leave balances automatically from credits, monthly accruals, approved leaves, carry-over and conversions. Employees and HR staff shall see the current balance per leave type and the history of transactions. Under Section 5.4, employees shall be able to download their own leave ledger for the current year as a PDF file.
features.route_reason: The feature clearly defines actors, outcomes, and data for leave balance management and reporting, which is common in HR software.
features.justification: Feature involves multiple leave balance computations, history tracking, and PDF ledger download, exceeding simple reference tables per rubric

args.query: leave balances computation and display with downloadable ledger PDF

features.name: Leave types and policies
features.description: HR staff shall configure leave types (vacation leave, sick leave, emergency leave, maternity, paternity, solo parent and special leaves for women, and leave without pay) with their entitlement rules: annual credits, monthly accrual, eligibility after regularisation, maximum carry-over and conversion of unused credits to cash at year-end.
features.route_reason: Configuring leave types and policies with entitlement rules is standard.
features.justification: admin_config rubric: several reference tables with validation and change history

args.query: configure leave types with entitlement rules including annual credits, monthly accrual, eligibility, carry-over, and conversion to cash

features.name: Performance and availability targets
features.description: The System shall support 300 concurrent users. Pages shall load within 3 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load. The System shall have at least 99.5% monthly availability, excluding scheduled maintenance.
features.route_reason: Performance and availability targets are measurable non-functional requirements.
features.justification: Rubric criterion for measurable target requiring work (load test to stated concurrency)

args.query: performance and availability targets 300 concurrent users 3 seconds page load 99.5% availability

features.name: Data from payroll
features.description: Payslip data produced by the payroll system shall be brought into the System so employees can view their payslips under Section 7.2.
features.route_reason: Standard integration to import payslip data for employee viewing is a common business software feature.
features.justification: Integration sizing rubric: two to four operations or file drop with retry and error logging

args.query: integration of payroll system payslip data for employee viewing

features.name: Data to payroll
features.description: At the end of every payroll cut-off, the System shall provide the Company's payroll system with each employee's approved attendance, overtime, night differential and leave data for that cut-off.
features.route_reason: Standard integration to export attendance and leave data to payroll system is a common business software feature.
features.justification: Matches rubric criterion for integration with file drop and retry/error logging (guideline-sizing_rubric_integration)

args.query: integration payroll attendance overtime night differential leave data

features.name: Reconciliation
features.description: The System shall keep a record of every data exchange with the payroll system, including the cut-off period, the number of employees and the status of the exchange.
features.route_reason: Logging and tracking data exchanges with payroll system is a common integration feature.
features.justification: Feature is a simple record-keeping of data exchanges without complex API calls or callbacks, matching S rubric criteria for integration.

args.query: integration data exchange record payroll system cut-off period number of employees status

features.name: Daily time record
features.description: The System shall compute each employee's daily time record from attendance logs and schedules: hours worked, lates, undertime, absences, overtime hours and night differential hours, taking approved leaves and holidays into account.

features.description: Employees shall file overtime requests before or after rendering overtime.

features.description: HR staff and branch supervisors shall maintain shift schedules and work rosters, including fixed, rotating and flexible shifts, rest days and schedule swaps. Schedules may be assigned per employee or per group and may be uploaded from a template.

assumptions: Client responsibility (p10): The Company shall assign a product owner from HR.
The System shall be hosted in a public cloud environment arranged by the vendor, with separate development, test (UAT) and production environments.
The System shall be accessible through current versions of common web browsers on desktop and mobile devices.
The complete employee records and current leave balances of all employees shall be available in the System from the first day of live operation.
Approvals shall be possible from a mobile browser.
Self-service functions shall be usable on mobile browsers, as most branch employees do not have Company computers.
The interface shall not require re-encoding by payroll staff.
The System shall seamlessly address all data privacy needs of the Company in an optimal manner.
The System shall be secure, user-friendly and scalable to support the Company's future growth.
Data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest.

exclusions.text: Payroll computation, withholding tax and statutory contribution processing remain in the Company's existing payroll system and are not part of this procurement.
Recruitment, learning management and performance appraisal modules are not part of this procurement.
Cloud subscription fees after turnover will be paid by the Company.
